name: Pennsylvania
tagline: From the Lake Erie shore to the Delaware, by way of Wilds lumber towns and Lancaster farm ridges.
intro: Pennsylvania's byways run along the Lake Erie shore and across the big woods of the northern tier, through anthracite and railroad valleys in the northeast, over the Laurel Highlands, and into the farm country and old battlefields of the south. This chapter follows the Pennsylvania Byways Program of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, which designates roads at the request of local governments; several older byways, including two interstate-grade freeways near Philadelphia, were instead named scenic byways by acts of the General Assembly, which also bars new billboards along them. The Longhouse loop in the Allegheny National Forest is listed separately because the Forest Service designated it.

members.name: The Great Lakes Seaway Trail
members.blurb: PA 5 keeps Lake Erie close across Erie County, within half a mile of the water at Lake City, then turns up Peninsula Drive toward Presque Isle and its lighthouse, with the Erie Maritime Museum down on the bayfront.

members.name: The Lake Wilhelm
members.blurb: Creek Road runs a few quiet miles through Maurice K. Goddard State Park in Mercer County, along the shore of Lake Wilhelm, a reservoir of some 1,680 acres where anglers and boaters put in.

members.name: Crawford Lakelands Byway
members.blurb: Back roads between Jamestown and Linesville circle Conneaut Lake, the largest natural lake in Pennsylvania, and reach Pymatuning, where ducks at the spillway walk across the backs of crowded schools of fish.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: The Kinzua
members.blurb: A short road through McKean County hardwoods leaves US 6 for Kinzua Bridge State Park, where a skywalk runs out along six steel viaduct towers left standing by a 2003 tornado, high above the Kinzua Gorge.

members.name: High Plateau
members.blurb: PA 144 crosses the top of the Allegheny plateau for 27 miles between Snow Shoe and Renovo, through Sproul State Forest with no houses or power lines in sight and an overlook kept for stargazers.

members.name: Bucktail Trail
members.blurb: PA 120 follows the West Branch Susquehanna from Lock Haven to Renovo, then climbs through Sproul and Elk state forests to Emporium, St. Marys and Ridgway, on a road named for a Civil War regiment of rangers.

members.name: West Branch Susquehanna River Byway
members.blurb: Some 72 miles of Clearfield County roads trace the West Branch Susquehanna between Karthaus and Cherry Tree, past the McGee's Mills covered bridge and the rock outcrops of Bilger's Rocks, with elk sometimes in the fields.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Governor Casey Byway
members.blurb: The US 6 expressway climbs the Lackawanna Valley from Dunmore toward Carbondale through old anthracite country, with Steamtown's locomotives and the Lackawanna Coal Mine tour within easy reach of the road.

members.name: Gateway to the Endless Mountains
members.blurb: A short run of Business Route 6 through the borough of Tunkhannock in Wyoming County, past the Dietrich Theatre, at the doorstep of the hill country the state calls the Endless Mountains.

members.name: Viaduct Valley Way
members.blurb: Some 37 miles of PA 92 and its neighbors between Dixon and Lanesboro wind through valley farms and bluestone quarry country, under the concrete Tunkhannock Viaduct and on to the old stone Starrucca Viaduct, still in railroad use.

members.name: Delaware River Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Seventeen miles of PA 611 and the Belvidere Highway follow the Delaware north from Easton to Riverton, through old river towns and farm fields, with Little Martin's Creek in the background for part of the way.

members.name: Blue Route
members.blurb: Twenty miles of I-476 from I-95 near Chester to the Turnpike at Plymouth Meeting, named for the blue line that won out on a 1958 planning map and laid through the Crum Creek valley.

members.name: Exton Bypass
members.blurb: The US 30 freeway around Exton in Chester County, finished in December 1995 and made a scenic byway by the legislature the following July, runs near the old Lincoln Highway and the American Helicopter Museum.

members.name: Brandywine Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: PA 52 and the old Creek Road wind through Brandywine Valley farm country in Chester County, past Longwood Gardens and the Brandywine River Museum, with old houses along the way tied to the Underground Railroad.

members.name: U.S. Route 202 Parkway
members.blurb: A parkway built for US 202 from Montgomery Township to Doylestown, opened in December 2012 with split-rail fences, landscaped verges and a side trail for walkers and cyclists winding beside it through fields and woods.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lebanon Cornwall Byway
members.blurb: PA 419 runs east from Quentin across Lebanon County to the Berks line, by way of the Cornwall Iron Furnace and Newmanstown, through Amish farm country within reach of the Middle Creek wildlife lands.
members.note: Shown on the map as Route 419 Scenic Byway.

members.name: Journey Through Hallowed Ground
members.blurb: In Pennsylvania the byway follows US 15 and Business 15 from the Maryland line up through Gettysburg and its battlefield, the northern end of a 180-mile route that runs south to Monticello in Virginia.

members.name: Conestoga Ridge Byway
members.blurb: PA 23 follows a ridge across eastern Lancaster County between Blue Ball and Morgantown, through the villages of Goodville and Churchtown, with Amish and Mennonite farms in the Conestoga valley below.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: The National Road
members.blurb: US 40 carries the old National Road across southwestern Pennsylvania from Maryland to West Virginia, past the Summit Inn and Fort Necessity battlefield, then down through Uniontown to cross the Monongahela at Brownsville.

members.name: Grand View
members.blurb: A short climb up McArdle Roadway to Grandview Avenue along the brow of Mount Washington, where the overlooks face downtown Pittsburgh and both the Monongahela and Duquesne inclines are close at hand.

members.name: Laurel Highlands
members.blurb: PA 711 and PA 381 run 68 miles from the Conemaugh River at Seward through Ligonier and Ohiopyle to the West Virginia line, past Frank Lloyd Wright's Fallingwater and the rafting water of Ohiopyle State Park.

members.name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway
members.blurb: Picking up the Tubman byway where Route 52 crosses from Delaware, this short Chester County route carries the Underground Railroad story onto quiet backroads where Quaker and Black abolitionists once aided freedom seekers.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Pennsylvania Route 6 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Pennsylvania's longest byway, 211 miles of US 6 across the northern tier from Warren past the Kinzua Bridge to Coudersport, then down Pine Creek through Galeton toward Wellsboro and the Pennsylvania Grand Canyon.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Longhouse National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 36-mile loop around the Kinzua Creek arm of the Allegheny Reservoir under oak and black cherry, crossing Cornplanter Bridge with side roads up to the Rimrock and Jakes Rocks overlooks.
